content.title: Duke University Names Kara Lawson As Its Women's Basketball Coach
content.text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JANUARY 09: Assistant coach Kara Lawson of the Boston Celtics passes the ball prior to the game against the Philadelphia 76ers at the Wells Fargo Center on January 9, 2020 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.Getty ImagesYesterday, Duke University named Kara Lawson as its fifth women’s basketball head coach. The former University of Tennessee guard and WNBA Champion had been an assistant coach with the NBA’s Boston Celtics before the announcement. In 2019, she became the first female coach in the Celtics’ 73-year history. "Well, it is a dream come true for me," said Lawson in a released statement. "I have wanted to be a coach since I was a kid. To have an opportunity to lead a group of young women at a prestigious university like Duke – I have run out of words; it is unbelievable and very exciting.”From 1999 to 2003, Lawson played under Hall of Fame coach Pat Summitt, where the Lady Vols advanced to NCAA championship games in 2000 and 2003. Following her storied All-SEC career, Lawson spent 13 seasons in the WNBA, where she led the Sacramento Monarchs to a championship in 2005. Since retiring from professional basketball, Lawson gained national attention as a collegiate studio analyst, and in 2017 she was the first female analyst for a nationally-televised NBA game.Lawson replaces Joanne P. McCallie, who announced her decision not to return for a 14th season after failing to receive a contract extension. “...Everybody I spoke with and had a chance to interact with, I immediately felt a great connection. It wasn't a decision based on emotion, but there was a lot of emotion involved in it because of how excited I am and how ready I am to get started and to work with the players."Lawson’s hiring comes at a critical time as there have been increased calls for diversity and inclusion among head coaches. She enters the ACC as its fifth Black head coach and the first in Duke’s history. Former WNBA players and long-time assistant coaches, Tina Thompson and Niele Ivey, are now head coaches at Virginia and Notre Dame, respectively. MORE FROM FORBES ADVISOR"A highly-seasoned champion at multiple levels within the basketball landscape, Kara Lawson is the ideal fit for Duke University," said athletic director Kevin White in a statement. "Throughout the process, it became abundantly clear that her authenticity, passion, contemporary vision and unwavering commitment to the student-athlete experience align seamlessly with the values of the institution. With her high degree of emotional intelligence, Kara's astute ability to connect with future, current and former student-athletes, as well as the passionate and dedicated supporters of Duke women's basketball, will have an immediate and profound impact on the entire program."
